_comment: The refusal register for the research database converter (tools/research_convert.py, AD-M37). The converter reads Matthew's workbook, the additions overlay and the design-id ledger, and refuses to write ANYTHING if one of these fires: a partial content set is worse than none. Grammar refusals keep their own G codes (grammar_codes.json); these are the X codes, for what sits around the grammar. Codes are never renumbered or reused; a new rule takes the next free number. Every code has at least one hostile case in tests/fixtures/research_convert/cases.json.

codes.summary: A sheet the converter reads is not in the workbook.
A column the converter reads is not in its sheet's header row.
A Year that is neither an integer nor a declared value (`base`). Never coerced, never defaulted (D5).
A nation name or code that overlay.nations does not declare, or a declared nation with no Start 1930 row.
A category code that is not on the Categories sheet, or a fold or fallback naming one.
An authored id appears twice in one table, or a name that must be unique (a design, a vendor, a bureau within its nation) appears twice.
Two different authored ids qualify to the same shipped id (lower case, '-' to '_'). Ids are never merged silently.
An authored id is both a technology and a doctrine, or a bureau name resolves in more than one nation where the token does not say which. Bare ids resolve by table membership, never by prefix.
A design or vendor name has no entry in the ledger. Run with --mint to append one, or append a rename entry by hand to keep an existing id (D4).

The ledger is malformed: an entry that is not exactly {id, name}, an id that is not pb:design_NNNN or pb:vendor_NNNN, or one name mapped to two ids. The ledger is append-only: the converter only ever appends to it (--mint).
A bureau marked active in the overlay has no capacity. Never defaulted (D3).
The overlay names a bureau, nation, flag, category, project or tag that the workbook and overlay do not declare.
The overlay has the wrong format line, an unknown key, or a value of the wrong type.

A cell outside the grammar (Base holders, Active from, Secondary, Tags, Exclusive with, a Type / role absent from overlay.design_roles) that does not match its declared form. The overlay may declare its reading; the converter never guesses.
The game's Content/vocabulary.json (passed as --vocabulary) cannot be read, or has no list of pools. Its pools are the only material currencies a study may cost.
The game's Content/pb/model.json (passed as --models) cannot be read. Its hand-authored models are the templates a generated design model copies its production cost and rate from (D29).

A design in the slice has the year 'base', and the overlay declares no readings.base_model_year. A model needs an integer year, and what that year MEANS is the engine's to say, so the converter never picks one.
codes.retired: D30, 2026-10-27: a model's year is HISTORICAL, so a base design ships year null and year_declared base exactly like its project, and no reading supplies a year. Nothing can raise this code; it stays so the number is never reused.

codes.summary: An active bureau has no home in overlay.bureau_homes, or a home is not {place, lon, lat} with lon in [-180, 180] and lat in [-90, 90]. A home is AUTHORED as a place and its coordinates (a fact, checkable against history); its province is DERIVED from the polygons, so a home the map does not reach ships province null and is reported, never refused (D39).

overlay.ai_research_weights lacks a nation x live-category weight, or a weight is not an integer >= 0. Every nation has a weight for every category that is not folded away (brief item 13; placeholders until the strategic AI exists).

The province polygons (--provinces), the authored facility points (--facilities) or the hex artifact the game loads (--map) cannot be read. They are the public pipeline data item 13 derives the province research value from, read and never copied.
